topIssues.title: Interop NUT bundle activation follow-ups (from #20723)
topIssues.author: maurelian
topIssues.body:
PR #20723 added the core Interop NUT bundle activation. This issue tracks review feedback from sebastianst that was scoped out of the merge to land the core work first. Each item links back to the original review thread.

## ~1. Restructure `interop_activation_diff_test.go` from Go unit test to bash script~

Done: b0b9eb6423b7


## ~2. Re-enable `TestInteropActivation_MultiChain` under kona~
- [discussion_r3325064396](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20723#discussion_r3325064396) — track action to re-enable the test under kona; check with the interop team what's missing.

Note: this is no longer relevant, as the test has been removed. Instead, follow up work will be needed to implement the test using devstack rather than e2e, for example - https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/op-acceptance-tests/tests/osaka_on_l2_test.go#L324.


## 3. ~`u128::MAX` vs `u256::MAX` for ETHLiquidity bootstrap mint~
- [discussion_r3325171409](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20723#discussion_r3325171409)

Note: Not an issue, as explained in the discussion this is the amount using in [L2Genesis](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/522bfb47ad0e2c279861f8b6964faac8b6bee4f8/packages/contracts-bedrock/scripts/L2Genesis.s.sol#L542) and the current [interop_upgrade_transactions.go](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/522bfb47ad0e2c279861f8b6964faac8b6bee4f8/op-node/rollup/derive/interop_upgrade_transactions.go#L49-L52) on develop, so we are just preserving that invariant.


## 4. Proofs-team sync on depset wiring

These four threads are the same architectural question viewed from different files:
- [discussion_r3325475684](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20723#discussion_r3325475684) — `op-program/client/boot/boot.go` (BootInfo.DependencySet field)
- [discussion_r3325480118](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20723#discussion_r3325480118) — `op-program/client/preinterop.go` (why pass dep set pre-interop?)
- [discussion_r3325483779](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20723#discussion_r3325483779) — `op-program/host/kvstore/local.go` (always require dep set?)
- [discussion_r3325526149](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20723#discussion_r3325526149) — `rust/kona/bin/client/src/single.rs` (auto-synth one-chain depset)
**Background:** the Rust `StatefulAttributesBuilder` constructor (`rust/kona/crates/protocol/derive/src/attributes/stateful.rs:64`) now refuses to construct without a `DependencySet` when `interop_time` is set, to prevent silent divergence from op-node on the activation-gate `len(depSet.Chains()) > 1`. Op-program (Go) enforces the same invariant. To satisfy it symmetrically we threaded the depset through:
- `BootInfo.DependencySet` populated from preimage (custom-chain) or `chainconfig.DependencySetByChainID` (registry) when interop is scheduled.
- `RunPreInteropProgram` passes it through — any chain with interop scheduled (even when running blocks before the activation) must carry the depset because the activation block itself reads it.
- `kvstore/local.go` serves `dependencySetKey` based on `s.config.DependencySet != nil` instead of the old `InteropEnabled` boolean flag (the flag and the data should always agree, but driving off the data is more honest).
- `kona-host single` auto-synthesises a one-chain depset from the rollup config when `interop_time.is_some()`, matching op-node's single-chain branch (`len(deps) > 1` evaluates to `false`) — the single subcommand is by construction about one chain, so a one-element depset is the truthful representation.
**Action:** sync with proofs team to confirm the design — particularly pre-interop chains carrying depset, and the single-chain client's auto-synthesis. All four threads resolve via this same sync.
## 5. ~CI clarity for `interop-deposits-dump` cargo run~
- [discussion_r3324566294](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20723#discussion_r3324566294) — Sebastian couldn't find the test run in CircleCI; questioned runtime and possible duplication with Go `derive` package tests.

Notes: The script was converted to bash as requested. The [full workflow run](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism?useNewPipelines=true&filter=branch%3Aequals%3Afeat%2Finterop-l2cm-nut&created_after=2026-05-15T00%3A00%3A00.000Z&created_preset=Last+2+weeks&selectedPipeline=gh%2Fethereum-optimism%2Foptimism%2F126780&workflowId=820cd91c-7d39-4b97-920a-61157e22c7ac&job=ef06c20d-1017-4b3d-ad73-bca762c479fd&buildNumber=5141348&jobType=build) takes about 4 minutes. I think that's fine since it runs in parallel, but we can work to improve it as follow up if need be.

---
**Plan:** `plans/2026-05-28-migrate-interop-activation-multichain-to-devstack.md` (covers item #2).
**Source PR:** #20723
**Suggested labels:** `A-interop`, `A-fault-proof`, `C-tech-debt`, `M-followup`

topPRs.title: [codex] batcher consensus proof of concept
topPRs.author: opsuperchain
topPRs.body:
## Summary

This draft PR adds a blob-mode-only batcher consensus proof of concept.

- adds a rollup config verifier address and batcher proof endpoint wiring
- attaches proof calldata to blob batcher transactions without changing blob batch data
- verifies blob transaction calldata in op-node derivation via block-hash `eth_call` to an L1 verifier contract and skips invalid proofs
- adds verifier logs, metrics, and unit coverage for batcher, derivation, L1 client, and verifier helpers
- adds DevStack verifier and sidecar options, valid/invalid acceptance tests, OP Up demo mode, and `op-up smoke-batcher-consensus`
- adds a Rust proof sidecar that runs Commonware Simplex over a simulated 4-validator network and emits the resulting finalization certificate
- switches the Simplex certificate scheme to Commonware secp256r1 so the certificate signatures are EVM-checkable
- carries a `CWSIMPLX1 || digest || marker || fixed POC envelope || Commonware certificate` calldata envelope for the Commonware sidecar path
- verifies the Commonware Simplex finalization certificate in the DevStack L1 verifier by checking the proposal digest, signer bitmap, quorum signatures, and P256 signatures over `sha256(union_unique(finalize_namespace, proposal.encode()))`
- activates Osaka on the DevStack L1 preset used by the Commonware verifier so the L1 `eth_call` path has the P256 precompile available
- makes the OP Up batcher-consensus demo self-contained by using the no-fault-proofs single-chain preset and adding `--l2-rpc-port` for running valid and invalid demo networks side by side

## POC Caveat

The current sidecar runs a deterministic in-process Commonware Simplex network for the POC. The verifier now directly checks the Commonware secp256r1 certificate signatures in EVM, but the certificate layout and validator set are still fixed for this proof of concept rather than a production configurable committee/verifier contract.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test --manifest-path op-batcher-consensus-sidecar/Cargo.toml

go test ./op-service/batchconsensus ./op-devstack/sysgo -run 'TestBuild|TestBatchConsensusMockVerifier|TestBuildCommonware|TestBuildSigned' -count=1 -v

DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND=op-geth RUST_JIT_BUILD=1 go test ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/batcher_consensus -run 'TestBatchConsensusValidProofAdvancesSafeHead' -count=1 -v

DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND=op-geth RUST_JIT_BUILD=1 go test ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/batcher_consensus -run 'TestBatchConsensusInvalidProofDoesNotAdvanceSafeHead' -count=1 -v

go test ./op-up -run '^$'
go run ./op-up --help
go run ./op-up smoke-batcher-consensus all --help

# live OP Up demo smoke, with one shell per long-running devnet:
DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND=op-geth RUST_JIT_BUILD=1 go run ./op-up --dir /tmp/op-up-batcher-consensus-valid --batcher-consensus-poc
DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND=op-geth RUST_JIT_BUILD=1 go run ./op-up --dir /tmp/op-up-batcher-consensus-invalid --batcher-consensus-poc --batcher-consensus-poc-invalid --l2-rpc-port 8546
go run ./op-up smoke-batcher-consensus all

git diff --check
```

The DevStack acceptance tests show valid Commonware consensus proof calldata advancing `local-safe`, and invalid proof calldata being rejected with `false batch consensus verifier result` while `local-safe` remains at genesis.

The live OP Up smoke run started a valid proof demo on `http://localhost:8545` and an invalid proof demo on `http://localhost:8546`; `smoke-batcher-consensus all` observed the valid safe head reach the submitted transfer block and the invalid safe head stay below the submitted transfer block for 20 seconds.

Note: the DevStack and OP Up runs used `DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND=op-geth` in this environment because op-reth was not built locally.

topPRs.title: op-up: add devstack preset devnet UX
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds a friendlier `op-up` UX for launching local op-devstack devnet presets.

This lets users run preset devnets from `op-up`, get randomized local RPC ports automatically, and see the information needed to interact with the network after startup.

## Changes

- Add `op-up up <preset>` / preset selection UX backed by op-devstack presets.
- Print service endpoints for L1/L2 EL, L2 CL, L1 beacon, and interop supernode RPC when available.
- Print deployed L1 contract addresses for each L2, including portal, system config, bridge, DGF, proxy admin, and delayed WETH.
- Use random local ports by default so users do not need to manually pick ports.
- Export devnet config files under `~/.op-up/configs/`, including endpoints, contracts, rollup configs, dependency set config, and generated JSON configs when available.
- Improve devstack temp-dir prefixes so op-up service logs/config artifacts are easier to identify by preset and service name.

topPRs.title: op-up: add devnet preset runner and control CLI
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds a friendlier `op-up` UX for launching local op-devstack devnet presets.

This lets users run preset devnets from `op-up`, get randomized local RPC ports automatically, and see the information needed to interact with the network after startup.

## Features

- Start realistic OP Stack devnets with one command.
- Pick from useful presets like minimal, interop, two-L2, multinode, conductors, and flashblocks.
- No manual port management: op-up finds ports and prints every endpoint.
- Get the funded test account, deployed contracts, L1 beacon RPC, L2 RPCs, and supernode RPC in one place.
- Export configs automatically for external tools like challenger/proposer runners.
- Control running services with start, stop, restart, and status.
- Simulate failures without editing presets or writing custom test code.
- Keep RPC endpoints stable across service restarts.
- Find service logs easily under ~/.op-up/logs.

## Changes

- Add `op-up up <preset>` / preset selection UX backed by op-devstack presets.
- Print service endpoints for L1/L2 EL, L2 CL, L1 beacon, and interop supernode RPC when available.
- Print deployed L1 contract addresses for each L2, including portal, system config, bridge, DGF, proxy admin, and delayed WETH.
- Use random local ports by default so users do not need to manually pick ports.
- Export devnet config files under `~/.op-up/configs/`, including endpoints, contracts, rollup configs, dependency set config, and generated JSON configs when available.

topPRs.title: chore(op-e2e): drop op-program references
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Decouples op-e2e from op-program so it can be deleted from the monorepo, part of ethereum-optimism/optimism#20276. After this PR, neither op-e2e nor op-devstack reference op-program.

- Moves the `engineapi` package (the in-process L2 engine used by action tests) from `op-program/client/l2/engineapi` into `op-e2e/actions/helpers/engineapi`.
- Stops deploying the legacy type-0 Cannon dispute game in the op-e2e deploy intent. It is no longer served by op-challenger, and it was the only reason op-e2e read `op-program/bin/prestate-proof-mt64.json`. The generic CannonKona (type 8) game still exercises the proof system.

Stacked on ethereum-optimism/optimism#21254 (Cannon game-type removal), which already cleared op-program out of op-devstack.

Test plan: `go test ./op-e2e/actions/helpers/engineapi/...` and `TestL2EngineAPI` pass; `just lint-go` clean.
